title: The queue is the synchronizer: post-surge prefix-cache hysteresis in agent serving is a convoy, and a dispatch-order change recovers the trapped engine without shedding
statement: Write the prefix-cache hit rate of a pool of agent sessions as a function of two things, not one: the working-set ratio $W/C$ (with $W = N c$ the aggregate context of the $N$ active sessions, $c$ tokens each, and $C$ the cache capacity in tokens, under least-recently-used (LRU) eviction, which discards the least recently referenced tokens first) and the dispersion of the sessions' call phases, read as the LRU stack distance in session units: for session $i$ let $K_i$ be the number of other sessions that made a call between $i$'s two consecutive calls, so $i$'s prefix is still cached if and only if $K_i\,c < C$; when a first-come-first-served (FCFS) prefill queue serves every waiting session once per round (lockstep), $K_i = N - 1$ for every call, while when the sessions' call times are independent renewal processes of equal rate (dispersed phases) $K_i \approx N(1 - e^{-\tau})$ with $\tau$ the session's own inter-call time in units of its mean, so that $$h_{\mathrm{lockstep}}(W/C) = \mathbb{1}\!\left[\tfrac{W}{C} \le 1\right], \qquad h_{\mathrm{dispersed}}(W/C) = \min\!\left(1, \tfrac{C}{W}\right),$$ two branches that differ by up to one full unit between $W = C$ and $W = 2C$, the band in which the card paper measured 0.81-0.93 hits in no-surge runs against 0.26-0.37 after a collapse at the same $W = 1.6$-$1.7\,C$ (sec. 5.2) and called the gap 'cache hysteresis'. Test, on the paper's own replay protocol (recorded Terminal-Bench coding-agent sessions replayed as closed loops with their tool gaps, Poisson arrivals, SGLang with the prefix radix cache on, one H100 pair in 1P1D or one colocated H100 as fallback), whether the post-surge deficit at matched $W/C$ is the phase term: reproduce the +100%-for-ten-minutes trap on a healthy base load, then at surge end apply one of five arms with arrivals unchanged except in the paper's own arm: (a) nothing; (b) one-shot phase jitter, every tool-idle session's next call held an extra $U(0, \tau_J)$ seconds once, $\tau_J$ twice the healthy-branch call cycle $L_0 + g$ ($L_0$ the unloaded call latency, $g$ the mean tool gap); (c) random dispatch order on the prefill queue for ten minutes (SGLang's shipped `--schedule-policy random`); (d) resident-first order (longest-prefix-match with its 128-request queue cutoff lifted, Basin's ordering lever alone); (e) the paper's recovery, arrivals cut to $0.3\lambda$ for ten minutes. Read, per arm and per minute from the engine counters and gateway timestamps, the hit rate, the empirical distribution of $K_i$ (the phase-dispersion ruler), $W/C$, and goodput over the following hour under the paper's definition (completed sessions per hour with slowdown at most 4 and at least 95% of decode steps inside the 50 ms inter-token-latency objective); step 0 is the same test on an LRU stack-distance replay of the recorded call orders, zero dollars.
claim: The post-surge hit-rate deficit at equal working set in agent serving is a convoy, not a cache-contents effect: the prefill queue has locked the sessions' call phases together so every prefix's stack distance is the whole population, and restoring phase dispersion (a one-shot jitter or a non-FCFS dispatch order) recovers the healthy branch at unchanged arrivals.
trick: In a cache that holds about one and a half pools' worth of context, whether a returning agent finds its prefix depends on how many other agents called in between; a queue makes that number 'everyone' for every call, so the cache stops working at half the load it could carry if the agents were out of step, and shuffling the order undoes it.
why_now: The card paper (2611.02543, 2026-11-02) is the first to measure the hysteresis at matched working set and to name the two branches as a fact: 'This is cache hysteresis: similar demand for cached context produces different hit rates because the cached contents differ.' (sec. 5.2), while its model 'uses the real-system hit-rate curve in Fig. 6b' (sec. 5.1), a one-dimensional curve in $W/C$ that cannot carry a second branch, so it sizes recovery from measured collapsed-state departures (0.20-0.31 of $\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}$) instead of predicting it. The instrument landed in September: KVSET (2609.27746, 2026-09-23) computes LRU stack distances of KV pages online with the Mattson stack algorithm and ships an open-source trace replayer; EfficientAgent (2609.33762, 2026-09-27) states the dispersed-phase working set in words, 'While one agent waits for its tool, the server processes the contexts of all other agents, so an agent's prefix is reused only if the host tier holds the reusable context of the whole agent pool', without the order term. The shipped behaviour makes the lockstep the default under exactly the backlog a trap creates: SGLang's scheduler default is `schedule_policy = 'fcfs'` and its longest-prefix-match option is switched off when the waiting queue exceeds 128 requests (`WAITING_QUEUE_PREFIX_MATCH_MAX = 128`; fetched from sglang/srt/managers/schedule_policy.py and arg_groups/fields/schedule.py, 2026-11-09). The two-branch law itself is the 1970 stack-distance result (Mattson, Gecsei, Slutz and Traiger) crossed with the 1979 convoy phenomenon (Blasgen, Gray, Mitoma and Price: a lock queue keeps processes in lockstep after the bottleneck clears); nothing newer is needed for the identity, and that is recorded as the flag.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 2 days): from recorded coding-agent trajectories with per-call prompt tokens, output tokens and tool gaps (the card's Terminal-Bench replay set if released; fallback: JetBrains-Research/the-complexity-trap SWE-agent tarballs or Open-SWE-Traces 2606.16038, the corpora C-W44-08 already names), run an LRU stack-distance simulation (KVSET's replayer or 200 lines) of $N$ closed-loop sessions at $W/C \in \{1.2, 1.4, 1.6, 2.0\}$ under three call orders — recorded Poisson phases, strict round-robin, and the order a saturated FCFS prefill queue would produce — and record $h$ and the $K_i$ distribution per order; compute the two-branch prediction at the card's trapped point ($W = 1.6$-$1.7\,C$: dispersed about 0.6, lockstep about 0). Step 1 (about 65 GPU-hours, 8 days): SGLang 1P1D on two H100s (fallback one colocated H100) serving a 30B-class FP8 open MoE (Qwen3-30B-A3B class; the card's Qwen3.6-35B-A3B if runnable), prefix radix cache on, replayer driving sessions as closed loops with recorded tool gaps and recorded output lengths (content discarded), Poisson arrivals, warm start as in the card (sec. 3); tune the base load so that a +100% ten-minute surge traps (about 3 runs of 2.5 h); then 5 arms x 2 seeded repeats x 2.5 h (arms (a)-(e) above, each applied at surge end), reading per minute the hit rate, $W/C$, the $K_i$ distribution from gateway call timestamps, and goodput over the hour after the surge. Readouts: the hit-rate-versus-$W/C$ scatter coloured by the median $K_i/(N-1)$ (one curve or two branches), the recovery sign per arm, and the time to the healthy branch.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead at step 0 if, at the trapped working set the hardware run reaches ($W/C$ read from counters), the dispersed-phase LRU replay also predicts a hit rate below 0.4: the post-collapse deficit is working set, not order, and the one-dimensional curve is right. Dead at step 1 if arms (b), (c) and (d) each leave the hit rate below 0.45 and goodput within 20% of arm (a) over the following hour while arm (e) recovers to within 20% of the pre-surge goodput: the hysteresis is in the cache contents or the population and not in the phases, the paper's account stands, and the negative result is a footnote (order control is not a recovery lever in prefix-cached agent serving). Pre-registered non-kill readings: if (c) and (d) recover but (b) does not, the convoy re-forms whenever a queue exists and the consequence is a scheduling default under backlog, not a one-time intervention; if (b) alone recovers, the trap is a one-shot synchronization and a gateway jitter at surge end is the whole fix.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.55: the trapped state sits at $W/C$ between 1.4 and 1.9 with median $K_i/(N-1)$ above 0.9 (every returning call finds the whole population in front of it), the no-surge branch at the same $W/C$ has median $K_i/(N-1)$ below 0.6; arms (c) and (d) lift the hit rate above 0.55 within ten minutes and goodput recovers to within 20% of pre-surge inside the hour at unchanged arrivals, arm (b) recovers in about half the runs (the convoy re-forms when the queue re-forms), arm (a) stays trapped, arm (e) recovers as the paper reports; the hit-rate scatter against $W/C$ separates into two branches by $K_i$ with the lockstep branch's cliff near $W = C$ and the dispersed branch's near $W \approx 1.9\,C$, which is where the card's Fig. 6b puts the forward cliff.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: A single hit-rate curve in $W/C$ with a contents-dependent offset after collapse: 'This is cache hysteresis: similar demand for cached context produces different hit rates because the cached contents differ.' (card, sec. 5.2); the model 'uses the real-system hit-rate curve in Fig. 6b' (sec. 5.1) and the recovery lever is fewer sessions: 'Once the cache collapses, low-reuse departure capacity sets the scale of the load reduction needed for recovery.' (abstract, fetched 2026-11-09); Basin's levers are admission on predicted peaks, lending and shedding, with ordering engaged 'under a persistent backlog' as a fixed arrival-plus-size priority (card, sec. 6), not as a de-synchronizer. The RL-side incumbents read the same collapse as capacity: MISA-T's hit rate 'collapses from 92.4% to 4.5%' at a permissive concurrency ceiling and TideRL's '~12%' under request-level batching (kill report CL-W43-12) are both at the lockstep branch's value, and both fix it by admitting fewer sessions.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If the two branches are real: the hit rate is a property of the dispatch protocol at fixed demand, every prefix-cache working-set planner (KVSET, EfficientAgent, 2610.22863) needs the order term beside capacity, the recovery lever in a trap is a scheduling flag rather than shedding, and the sustainable session count at a given cache is up to about $1.9\times$ higher under dispersed phases than under the FCFS default — which re-reads the RL rollout collapses (MISA-T 4.5%, TideRL 12%) as queue effects that pacing could fix without lowering concurrency. If one curve: the paper's account holds, order control is not a lever, and the stack-distance planners are complete as they stand.

scorecard.target_value: In print: the card paper states the hysteresis as a measured fact and attributes it to contents ('similar demand for cached context produces different hit rates because the cached contents differ', sec. 5.2) while its model has no state for order or contents and falls back to measured collapsed-state departures to size recovery (card, load_bearing_assumption); EfficientAgent 2609.33762 writes the dispersed-phase working set in words ('an agent's prefix is reused only if the host tier holds the reusable context of the whole agent pool') and KVSET 2609.27746 ships the stack-distance instrument, neither with a synchronization term. Who pays: SGLang and vLLM maintainers choosing the prefill scheduling default under backlog (SGLang: `fcfs`, with longest-prefix-match disabled above 128 waiting requests, fetched 2026-11-09); gateway builders (Basin, Continuum, ThunderAgent) choosing between admission and ordering; RL-infra teams (MISA-T, TideRL, VenusRL) whose hit-rate collapses sit at the lockstep value and who pay for them in concurrency caps.

impact_ceiling.floor: A two-GPU reproduction of the card's trap with the mechanism isolated by the order arms and the two-branch law written down; cited by Basin's and EfficientAgent's follow-ups as the order term. Requires step 1. Judgment p 0.5.
impact_ceiling.middle: The hit-rate curve of prefix-cached agent serving re-stated as two branches with phase dispersion as the state variable; KV working-set planners add the order axis and one engine documents a non-FCFS default under backlog; CL-W43-12's rollout collapses re-read as queue effects. Requires step 1 positive on both (c) and (d) and one maintainer to pick it up. Judgment p 0.25.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: 'The queue is the synchronizer' becomes the standard account of cache metastability in agent serving and RL rollout: where $1 < W/C < 2$, order control replaces admission caps and raises sustainable concurrency at equal cache by up to about $1.9	imes$, confirmed at cluster scale by a lab. Judgment p 0.08.

scorecard.relevance: L3 routes (Lloyd / Netravali / Tri Dao): direct, a systems measurement with a mechanism and a configuration consequence on a rollout and serving engine. Industry: serving and RL-infra teams. title: Predict the peak or read the present: Basin's size predictor against current-context admission with hysteresis, on the same hardware
statement: Run, on one SGLang prefill-decode (PD) deployment (1P3D on four H100s or H200s, the card's topology) with the card's replayed Terminal-Bench sessions under two of its surge scenarios, four gateways that differ only in the admission quantity: (i) no admission, first-come-first-served (the Continuum anchor); (ii) working-set admission on the sessions' current contexts with the card's hysteresis (engage at $B_0$, release below $\alpha_R B_0$ after a cool-down, the page-fault-frequency budget adaptation on) — the rule the card's hardware prototype ran; (iii) the same budget with each session reserved at its predicted peak context $\hat W_i$ from the card's cross-fitted ridge regression on task text and first-prompt length (rank correlation 0.56-0.64 in the card) and the fixed arrival-plus-size priority $p_i = a_i + \hat W_i / r$; (iv) the same with the exact recorded peak (the oracle), lending and shedding off in all four so that admission is the only difference. Measure goodput under the card's definition (completed sessions per hour with slowdown at most 4 and at least 95% of decode steps inside the 50 ms inter-token-latency objective), hit rate and parked time, and report the ratios $G_{(iii)}/G_{(ii)}$ and $G_{(iv)}/G_{(ii)}$ with two seeded repeats per cell.
claim: On hardware, reserving each agent session's predicted peak context adds under 5% goodput over admitting on the context it has now with hysteresis, and the exact-peak oracle adds under 15%: the paper's simulated 1.27-1.35x oracle headroom is a property of the reservation design, and the predictor is a forecaster that an observation rule matches.
trick: Instead of guessing how big each agent's conversation will get and reserving that much cache up front, admit agents while the cache has room and stop when it does not; on real hardware the guess should buy nothing, because the paper's own real-hardware result was obtained without it.
why_now: The card paper (2611.02543, 2026-11-02) split its own evidence across two systems: 'The hardware prototype uses arrival-time ordering and current-context admission (§6.6); the predictor-driven controller is evaluated in simulation from §7.3 on.' (sec. 7.2), on a simulator that 'For the composition, it predicts 2.6 $\times$ the measured goodput.' (sec. 7.10); the headroom it attributes to prediction is simulated only: 'Supplying exact peak contexts raises goodput by 1.27–1.35 $\times$ in the plotted scenarios and 1.10–1.51 $\times$ across triggers, showing further benefit from improved predictions.' (sec. 7.9). The same-system comparison is therefore unrun by the paper's own sentences. The observation-versus-prediction question is live in the lane: FluidPD 2610.06917 and ConServe 2606.01839 argue 'observation, not prediction' for role reassignment in serving (CL-W43-08 thread), and the card's own hardware number (1.20-1.70x Continuum at real H200 1P3D) came from the observation rule.

killing_experiment.design: Build the gateway (about four days): an admission layer in front of the SGLang router holding per-session context, the card's budget rule $\sum_{j \in \mathrm{res}} \hat W_j + \hat W_i \le B$ with $\hat W$ set either to the current context (arm ii), the ridge prediction (arm iii) or the recorded peak (arm iv), hysteresis constants from the card ($m = 0.9$, $\alpha_R = 0.8$, cool-down, $\Delta = 30$ s), fixed priority $p_i = a_i + \hat W_i / r$ with $r = 30$ tokens per second in arms (iii) and (iv), FCFS in (i) and (ii); the predictor refit by the card's recipe (per-workload ridge on TF-IDF of task text plus log lengths, leave-one-trajectory-out) and its rank correlation reported before any serving run. Serve a 30B-class FP8 open MoE in 1P3D on four GPUs, prefix radix cache on, the replayer driving recorded sessions as closed loops with recorded tool gaps and output lengths, Poisson arrivals, warm start; two scenarios (the +100% ten-minute surge on a healthy base load; a sustained load at 0.9 of the profiled peak departure rate), two seeded repeats, 2 h each: 4 arms x 2 scenarios x 2 repeats x 2 h x 4 GPUs = 128 GPU-hours plus 16 for calibration. Readouts: goodput ratios with the repeats' range, hit rate, parked time, the share of admitted sessions whose actual peak exceeded the budget under arm (ii) (the over-admission the predictor is meant to prevent), and the oracle gap $G_{(iv)}/G_{(iii)}$ against the paper's simulated 1.27-1.35x.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead if $G_{(iii)}/G_{(ii)} \ge 1.15$ in both scenarios with the two repeats' ranges separated: per-session size prediction is a lever beyond observation in agent-serving admission, and the negative result is the first hardware measurement of what a text predictor of peak context is worth (a citable footnote either way). Pre-registered non-kill readings: if $G_{(iv)}/G_{(ii)} \ge 1.25$ while $G_{(iii)}/G_{(ii)} < 1.05$, prediction would pay if it were good and the current predictor is not — the paper's sec. 7.9 reading, confirmed on hardware; if $G_{(iv)}/G_{(ii)} < 1.05$, the oracle headroom is a simulator artifact and the reservation design, not prediction quality, is the open question.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.55: $G_{(iii)}/G_{(ii)} \in [0.97, 1.05]$ in both scenarios, $G_{(iv)}/G_{(ii)} \in [1.02, 1.12]$; arm (ii) over-admits in 10-20% of admissions (sessions whose peak later exceeds their current context by more than the margin) but the page-fault-frequency adaptation lowers $B$ before the hit rate leaves its plateau, so the over-admission costs little; arm (iii)'s fixed priority delays large sessions and raises their slowdown-violation share, offsetting its admission gain.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: That peak-context prediction is the admission lever and better prediction is the path: 'Supplying exact peak contexts raises goodput by 1.27–1.35 $\times$ in the plotted scenarios and 1.10–1.51 $\times$ across triggers, showing further benefit from improved predictions.' (card, sec. 7.9); 'reserves their predicted peak contexts against an adaptive admission budget' (abstract, fetched 2026-11-09). MISA-T 2608.11152 likewise estimates KV demand per workload class for its admission caps (kill report CL-W43-12). The counter-position exists only for role switching: FluidPD and ConServe (serving) argue observation over prediction; nobody has run it for session admission.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If the predictor adds nothing on hardware: Basin's measured contribution is a Denning working-set rule on current context with hysteresis, the text predictor leaves the recipe, the simulated 1.20-2.05x is re-read, and 'observe, don't predict' extends from PD role switching (CL-W43-08's sentence) to session admission — a second control loop for the same claim shape. If the predictor adds 15% or more: the first hardware number for per-session size prediction in agent serving, and the question becomes a harness-declared cap (the card's information_asymmetry (2)) rather than a text regression.

scorecard.target_value: In print: the card paper's own split ('The hardware prototype uses arrival-time ordering and current-context admission (§6.6); the predictor-driven controller is evaluated in simulation from §7.3 on.', sec. 7.2) and its simulator's error on compositions ('it predicts 2.6 $\times$ the measured goodput', sec. 7.10); the lane's standing question whether observation matches prediction in rollout and serving control (CL-W43-08: Prorsa reports forecast error without the throughput it costs; FluidPD and ConServe argue observation). title: What top-k cannot price it can still rank: the kernel fixed-size retrieval leaves is orthogonal to every swap a memory store makes
statement: Take the card's design: $T$ episodes, a store of $n$ memories, retrieved sets $S_t$ of fixed size $k$, outcome $r_t$, dividends $\theta_B$ (the value a set $B$ creates jointly beyond its proper subsets) up to resolution $d$, design matrix $(\mathbf{X}_d)_{tB} = \mathbb{1}[B \subseteq S_t]$, and Theorem 1's kernel vectors $\mathbf{h}_B = \sum_{j \notin B} \mathbf{e}_{B \cup \{j\}} - (k - |B|)\,\mathbf{e}_B$ for $|B| < d$, the 'invisible changes' that leave every episode's expected outcome unchanged and make every Shapley value $\varphi_i$ undetermined. Every decision a store makes under the same fixed-$k$ retriever — delete $i$ (the retriever then fills the slot with some $r_t$), keep $i$ over $j$, merge, choose which to retrieve — changes episode $t$ from $S_t$ to a same-size set $S_t'$, and the expected effect of that swap is the linear functional $\mathbf{x}_{S_t'} - \mathbf{x}_{S_t}$ with $(\mathbf{x}_S)_B = \mathbb{1}[B \subseteq S]$; a two-line check gives $$(\mathbf{x}_{S'} - \mathbf{x}_{S})^{\top}\mathbf{h}_B = 0 \quad \text{for every } B \text{ with } |B| < d \text{ and every } |S'| = |S| = k,$$ so the whole family of kernel vectors that fixed size creates is orthogonal to the effect of every same-size swap: what top-$k$ leaves undetermined is exactly the part of memory value no top-$k$ decision depends on, and at $d = 1$ the determined differences $\theta_{\{i\}} - \theta_{\{j\}}$ (contrasts, in the design-of-experiments sense of a comparison whose coefficients sum to zero) are the whole decision-relevant content. Measure two things on the card's public setup (pooled HotpotQA, $n = 2{,}971$, $T = 7{,}200$, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 cosine retrieval, gemini-2.5-flash-lite reader at temperature 0, exact match): the fraction $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ of pairwise contrasts $\mathbf{e}_{\{i\}} - \mathbf{e}_{\{j\}}$ determined under plain top-$k$ (the card's kernel test $\|\mathbf{U}^{\top}\mathbf{c}\| \le \tau \|\mathbf{c}\|$ with $\mathbf{U}$ an orthonormal basis of $\ker \mathbf{X}_1$ and $\tau = 10^{-8}$, among memories retrieved at least five times), beside the card's $0.001$ fraction of levels; and the real-data retention test the card left incomplete — rank memories by the reward average $\bar r_i$ (mean outcome of episodes retrieving $i$), by LEDGER's determined values on its own size-varying log, by the ridge contrast estimate on the top-$k$ log, by retrieval frequency and at random, keep 30% of the store, and score 300 held-out questions under the same retriever, paired per question.
claim: The memory value that top-$k$ retrieval leaves undetermined is the component no fixed-size decision reads: every same-size swap's expected effect is orthogonal to the kernel that fixed size creates, so contrasts between memories are determined by the logs the field already has, and changing retrieval to identify levels (LEDGER's 2.6-point price) buys a store nothing it can act on.
trick: If every answer is written with exactly k memories in hand, raising every memory's worth by one and lowering the baseline by k changes nothing anyone observes — and also changes nothing anyone decides, because every decision is a swap of one memory for another at the same k, and swaps only see differences.
why_now: The card paper (2611.03289, 2026-11-02) names the kernel and leaves the decision question open in its own words: 'the history fixes only the differences between values' (card, information_asymmetry), 'the pre-registered real-data retention test was not completed.' (F.7), and on synthetic logs 'the retained store succeeds in 5.52 of 300 evaluation episodes under LEDGER against 7.14 under reward averaging and 6.48 under the true Shapley values' (card, weakest_component (4)) — the true levels rank a worse store than the associational average, which is the sign the claim predicts; its remedy's cost is stated: 'Its effect on accuracy depends on the corpus, from $-2.6$ to $+2.7$ points, and the only rule that removes the cost is an oracle that needs gold labels.' (H.4). Causal Memory Policy (2610.02070, v3 2026-10-01, fetched abstract) reaches the retention side from the positivity direction: 'identified memory utility alone is insufficient for retention decisions: per-query utility reaches 0.78 AUC on the query for which it is estimated, yet no aggregation available to a retention policy predicts a memory's value on unseen queries.' Three identifiability-of-memory-utility papers in five weeks (CMP, LEDGER, 2611.03930 on 2026-11-02) make the question live and the window short; the identity itself is Scheffé-era (only contrasts are estimable in a one-way layout whose intercept is confounded), recorded as the flag.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 2 days): the two-line orthogonality proof written out for all $|B| < d$ (the three cases $B \subseteq S \cap S'$, $B \subseteq S$ only, $B \subseteq S'$ only); then, on the card's public setup, regenerate the plain top-$k$ log at $k = 5$ for $T = 7{,}200$ (24 passes over 300 questions, the card's protocol; about 7,200 reader calls of about 6K tokens, under $10 on gemini-2.5-flash-lite) and LEDGER's size-varying log with sizes $\{3, 5, 8\}$ and $\rho = 0.4$ (five seeds, as the card), unless the author's logs are released with the anonymous code; compute $\ker \mathbf{X}_1$ for each log, $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ among memories with $f_i \ge 5$, the kernel dimension, and the share of the kernel explained by $\mathbf{h}_\emptyset$ against aliasing vectors $\mathbf{e}_{\{i\}} - \mathbf{e}_{\{j\}}$ (identical columns) and private-store structure. Step 1 ($20, 3 days): the retention test — five rankings (reward average, LEDGER values, top-$k$ ridge contrasts with one representative of the undetermined coset, frequency, random), keep 30% of the 2,971-memory store, 300 held-out questions scored with the same retriever and reader in one launch window, three retention seeds for the random arm, paired bootstrap over questions (10,000 resamples).
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead if $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ under plain top-$k$ is below 0.20 while LEDGER's log gives above 0.60 among the same memories: the kernel is mostly aliasing and private-store structure that only size variation breaks, and the remedy is needed for decisions too. Dead also if the LEDGER-value ranking beats the top-$k$ contrast ranking in retention by at least 3 accuracy points with the paired interval excluding zero: the level bought a better store. Pre-registered uninformative reading: if all five rankings are within 2 points of random at 30% retention, retention on this corpus is insensitive to ranking (CMP's finding that no aggregation predicts value on unseen queries) and the retention clause is void while the kernel clause stands or falls on $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ alone.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.6: $F_{\mathrm{pair}} \ge 0.6$ among memories retrieved at least five times under plain top-$k$ at $T = 7{,}200$ against the card's $0.001$ for levels, with the kernel dimension small and dominated by $\mathbf{h}_\emptyset$ plus aliased gold-passage pairs; in retention, reward average and top-$k$ contrasts within 2 points of each other and both at or above LEDGER's values, all three 3-8 points above random, reproducing the synthetic ordering of F.7 on real data.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card's headline and remedy: 'top-$k$ retrieval leaves every memory value undetermined, however many episodes are logged' (abstract, fetched 2026-11-09), fixed by retrieving 'so that the next log determines more' at a measured accuracy cost, and the proposal that benchmarks report the fraction of values determined; RoMeRL, Memory-R2 and FadeMem (card neighbours) each score or learn per-memory values from fixed-size logs as if levels mattered; CMP 2610.02070 says identified utility does not aggregate to retention value. Nobody in the fetched set says that the undetermined direction is decision-irrelevant.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If true: memory systems keep top-$k$ and lose nothing a retention, merge or retrieval policy can use; the 'fraction of values determined' column is replaced by the fraction of contrasts determined, or dropped; the 2.6-point price of LEDGER's rule is paid only when the store-size decision (retrieve at all, or how many) is on the table, which is exactly when $k$ varies and the level becomes identified anyway; and for RL memory agents the rewards fix the within-group contrasts GRPO-style objectives use, so the card's 'fixed by the learner and not by the rewards' sentence applies to the level only. If false: the kernel under real top-$k$ logs is wide (aliasing, private stores), contrasts are undetermined too, and LEDGER's remedy is necessary for ranking, not only for pricing.

scorecard.target_value: In print: the card leaves the decision consequence open ('the pre-registered real-data retention test was not completed.', F.7; 'Finding at query time the questions where spreading retrieval costs nothing is the open problem that remains.', sec. 6) and its synthetic retention test ranks the truth below the average (5.52 against 7.14 of 300, F.7); CMP 2610.02070 states the retention gap from the other side ('identified memory utility alone is insufficient for retention decisions'). Who pays: memory-system builders (Mem0-, Letta-, FadeMem-class forgetting and retention) deciding whether to change retrieval in response to the card; memory-benchmark owners deciding whether to add the proposed determined-fraction column; RL memory-agent authors (RoMeRL, Memory-R2) reading the card's 'fixed by the learner' sentence.

identifiability: The determined-contrast fraction is a deterministic function of the log's design matrix, hence of the retrieval protocol and nothing else; it is computed before any outcome is read, as the card's audit is, and the claim is explicitly that a property of the protocol (fixed size) voids a component that the same protocol never reads. Resolution: the orthogonality holds at every $d$ for Theorem 1's family; the contrast statement about Shapley values is a $d = 1$ statement (at $d \ge 2$ the vectors $\mathbf{h}_{\{i\}}$ move Shapley contrasts, while swap effects stay orthogonal), which is the resolution of every real-data number in the card. Scope: aliasing vectors $\mathbf{e}_{\{i\}} - \mathbf{e}_{\{j\}}$ and private-store kernels are not created by fixed size and do void swaps between the aliased pair; $F_{\mathrm{pair}}$ measures how much of the real kernel is $\mathbf{h}_\emptyset$ and how much is these.
